questions.stem: In the stock trading greedy algorithm, how does the operational constraint of 'one transaction' differ from 'infinite transactions' regarding profit calculation?
options: One maximizes total volume traded; infinite minimizes the number of days held
One ignores price fluctuations; infinite only considers the first and last day
One requires holding until the final day; infinite allows immediate reversal
One seeks global min-max spread; infinite sums all positive daily gains
questions.correctAnswer: One seeks global min-max spread; infinite sums all positive daily gains

stemAnswerAlignment.responsivenessAnalysis: The stem asks for the difference in operational constraints/profit calculation between 'one transaction' and 'infinite transactions'. The keyed option (D) correctly identifies that the single transaction strategy seeks the global minimum-maximum spread (buy lowest, sell highest), while the infinite transaction strategy sums all positive daily gains (buy yesterday, sell today if price rises). This directly answers the comparative question.

questions.concept: Multiple Spanning Trees (System Invariants & Bug Diagnostics)
questions.stem: When constructing a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) for a connected undirected graph with V vertices, why must the resulting structure contain exactly V-1 edges?
options: To maintain connectivity between all vertices while strictly avoiding any cycles.
To satisfy the requirement that every vertex has a degree of at least one.
To ensure the total edge weight remains the absolute minimum possible.
To allow the greedy algorithm to terminate after exactly V iterations.
questions.correctAnswer: To maintain connectivity between all vertices while strictly avoiding any cycles.

stemAnswerAlignment.responsivenessAnalysis: Option A directly explains that a tree with V vertices must have V-1 edges to maintain connectivity while avoiding cycles, which is the reason for the edge count.

questions.stem: In the infinite transactions stock profit algorithm, why does the loop iterate only up to n-1 and compare prices[i] with prices[i+1]?
options: To prevent the algorithm from incorrectly identifying a cycle in the price data
To ensure the algorithm terminates before reaching the final array index
To calculate the global maximum profit by finding the difference of all elements
To capture every upward trend by summing profits from consecutive daily increases
questions.correctAnswer: To capture every upward trend by summing profits from consecutive daily increases

stemAnswerAlignment.responsivenessAnalysis: Option D directly explains that the loop compares each consecutive price pair to capture every upward trend, which answers the 'why' of the loop bound and comparison.
